dismissals.because: src/forge/close.py:220 a file git ignores is never committed, so it never reaches the pull request and can't leave the upgrade's committed files stale; the check compares what the pull request carries

findings.body: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` omits ignored, untracked files. If a client ignores a generated path newly added by the pinned release, `forge sync` creates it in the temporary worktree, but it remains absent from the commit and `stale` is empty. Close can then report Ready with a missing synced file. `sync.write` writes generated paths at `src/forge/sync.py:264-275`; compare those paths explicitly with the commit so ignore rules cannot hide them.
findings.title: Not done: An upgrade is not ready while synced files are out of date

findings.body: Running the full `forge sync` command also calls `install_shims` (`src/forge/sync.py:322`). Its hook paths are in the Git hooks directory shared by every worktree (`src/forge/githooks.py:46-50`), and `install_shims` can rewrite or rename those hooks (`src/forge/sync.py:278-307`). Thus checking a stale upgrade can change the real repository's hooks before close refuses it. Compare generated files in the scratch checkout without installing hooks.
findings.title: Keep the close comparison from rewriting shared Git hooks

findings.body: `mkdtemp()` creates a parent directory, but the cleanup removes only its `sync` worktree and branch. Every upgrade close leaves an empty temporary directory behind. Clean up the parent after removing the worktree.
findings.title: Remove the temporary parent directory after the sync check
